notes: Source frames are only 256x192 and stored rotated 90 degrees. I rotated each one upright, upscaled it, and cut ~25 zoomed crops to read small items; everything below was judged from those, not from the contact sheet.

These 18 frames do not all show one room. Roughly: 00 = a poster lying on a wood floor; 01-04 = a seating area with a white-brick chimney breast opening onto a dining/kitchen; 05-06 = a wall with two blind-covered windows and radiators; 07-14 = a living room with a black cast-iron fireplace, a wall-mounted TV and an open wooden staircase; 15-16 = a dark charcoal wall panel with framed watercolours; 17 = a hallway doorway looking into a bedroom. Counts are totals across everything visible, and room_type reflects the dominant space.

The two brown sofas differ in colour, arm shape and dressing (tan with a grey pom-pom throw in 01-04 vs darker brown with cream/navy cushions in 10-13), so I counted 2. I cannot fully rule out one sofa restyled, but the capture is a single ~140 s walk, so restaging is unlikely.

The pale blue-grey fringed rug in 03/04 and the dark teal-and-gold fringed rug in 07 have the same Berber motif vocabulary (zigzag chain, diamonds, triangles) and may well be one rug under very different exposure. I counted 2 with low confidence.
The brass diamond-mesh object on the floor in frame 07 has an arched top rail and scrolled feet; a fireplace spark guard is the best reading, but a magazine rack is possible.

Frames 05 and 06 show the same pair of windows, not four. Each sill carries a snake plant; the right sill additionally has a cactus and a white ceramic elephant, which are occluded by palm fronds in frame 05, so I did not list them for that frame.

Small wall pictures could not be counted exactly. The dining-area wall carries roughly four to five small prints plus round straw discs; I listed the two charcoal-wall watercolours separately because they are unambiguous.
The poster print in frame 00 is the same sheet visible on the floor near the door in frame 10 and in the hallway in frame 17 (verified by zooming: white paper, blue field, red banner).
Frame 13 is heavily occluded by the staircase; the TV, soundbar, sideboard, display cabinet and brown sofa are visible only through the treads, confirmed by zoom.

Deliberately excluded: walls, floors, ceilings, the white brick facing, garden furniture seen outdoors through the patio door, kitchen worktop clutter too blurred to name, and a small black rack at the bottom-left corner of frame 08 that I could not identify.
